A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MagicFuse, and their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material. All pages were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original visual-quality and segmentation experiments, cross-dataset generalization, component ablations and Cityscapes results in Section 3.

after.justification: v2 retains the work's original comparative experiments, generalization results, ablations and Cityscapes segmentation outcomes in Section 3.

M1.justification: Section 2.4 changes the stated visual objective from an unweighted sum of contrast, texture and color losses to a sum weighted by λ1, λ2 and λ3. This is a limited objective-specification revision; unspecified coefficient values prevent establishing an actual numerical weighting change. The architecture, fusion procedure, training stages and inference remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions train the diffusion branches using MFNet, FMB and LLVIP, evaluate visual and semantic representations on MFNet and FMB, and retain the Cityscapes experiment. No dataset, task or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The nine external fusion baselines remain unchanged. However, v2 removes the IKR-enhanced Ours-En. VIS comparator from the main MFNet semantic comparison in Table 3 and Figure 4. This comparator remains in the FMB comparison and as Model IV in the ablation study.

E3.justification: The stated splits, metrics, model sizes, optimizers, learning rates, batch sizes and diffusion-step counts match. These include MFNet's 1,177 training and 392 test images, FMB's 280 test images, and Cityscapes' 490/154 training/test counts. No revised experimental setting or rerun is established.

E4.justification: The same five-value τ sweep, four component ablations and cross-dataset generalization analyses are retained. Section 3.5 is edited and its figures reformatted, but the tested questions and supporting ablation evidence remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed lists, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports module FLOPs of 50.74G, 773.7G and 83.60G in Table 2. Retained benchmark and ablation scores, including Cityscapes' 65.80 versus 66.91 mIoU, are unchanged. The omitted Table 3 IKR-only result of 57.18 mIoU remains available as Model IV in Table 7.

T1.justification: v2 removes v1's explicit forward/reverse diffusion equations, noise-prediction objective and associated variance definitions in Section 2.2, replacing them with cited prose. Section 2.4 generalizes the visual-loss definition to weighted components and explicitly formulates cross-entropy over pixels and categories. No new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims: single-image knowledge-level fusion, complementary IKR/CKG branches, joint visual-semantic reinforcement, and performance competitive with multimodal fusion methods. The rewritten conclusion does not alter their scope.

C2.justification: The branch-role explanations, argument about preventing fusion-weight collapse, interpretations of generalization, and qualification that excessive cross-spectral influence can disrupt visible information remain substantively unchanged. No new applicability boundary or limitation is introduced.

D1.justification: v2 adds a public-code availability statement and repository address in the abstract, plus module-level FLOPs in the implementation table. Existing hardware and training details match. The newly introduced visual-loss coefficients are described but their values are not supplied; repository contents were not inspected.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ho et al.'s Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models as reference 4 and removes v1 references 10, 17 and 23, which supported application examples. The central research positioning and discussion of competing fusion methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 condenses the diffusion explanation, clarifies loss notation, and rewrites portions of the ablation discussion, Cityscapes description and conclusion. It also adds acknowledgments. The overall section sequence and most of the narrative are retained.

P2.justification: v2 revises Figure 2's rendering, redraws Figure 7's labels and legends, compacts semantic and ablation image grids, and relocates several displays. The implementation table gains a FLOPs column; Tables 1/2 and Figures 5/6 exchange numbering. Most displayed evidence is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves reporting through computational-cost disclosure, a code-access pointer, clearer pixelwise loss notation and more readable sensitivity plots. The empirical support remains unchanged. These gains are limited by unspecified visual-loss weights and reduced self-contained diffusion detail, but provide a small overall improvement in transparency and exposition.
